recipes.name: Black Beans
ingredients_raw: 2 cups dry black beans, soaked overnight
1 quart cold water, or as needed

steps.text: In a medium stockpot, combine soaked beans (see Editor's Note), water, onion, green pepper, garlic, bay leaves, salt, cumin and oregano. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat; reduce heat to low. Simmer, covered, until beans are tender, about 1 hour. Stir occasionally and add water as necessary so that the beans don't dry out or scorch.
When beans are tender, stir in wine, vinegar, and olive oil.

raw_recipe.headline: Black Beans
raw_recipe.description: Black beans cooked with onion, green pepper and garlic, seasoned with bay leaves, salt, cumin, and oregano. White wine and vinegar give these beans a nice little bite.

review.reviewBody: This recipe calls for dried beans soaked for all night... I always use dried beans but use a quick soak method. This would eliminate the salt making the beans "tough". The quick soak is simply: rinse dried beans in colander. Put dried beans into a stock pot covered with water, bring to boil (with lid off), boil for three minutes. After they've boiled the three minutes let soak for only one hour, with the lid on. A lot can be done in an hour! When the hour is over rinse again & proceed with your recipe. I've never had a problem with this method. And it actually helps to eliminate the problem (gas) most people associate with beans. I doubled this recipe today & we are already enjoying it! Very good flavor. I did add some more spices though, not too many.
These beans were delicious until I added the vinegar and wine. Leave those two out and these beans get 5 stars!
I would give this a 4.5 if I could. It was very good but I didn't add the last 3 ingredients: wine, vinegar, and oil.

Great recipe. Made this as a side dish. Scaled up to use whole bag of beans. Did quick soak and drained. Substituted chicken broth for water. Crushed garlic cloves. Used small crock pot and cooked on high for about 5hrs until beans were tender adding broth as needed to just cover. Omitted wine and vinegar and this came out great.
I omitted the wine, vinegar and olive oil as I wanted to freeze the beans for future use. I used a 2 lb bag of beans and made them in my slow cooker. Very nice seasoning combo.

So easy ! Just use canned organic black beans, I don't have the time to do all the boiling etc. you can get this ready in 20min. Just sauté some yellow pepper a half of chopped onion and some garlic and oil . And a teaspoon of cumin , tsp of oregano , add your drained beans add a little oil and some organic apple cider vinegar and it's pretty yummy! Sprinkle with fresh cilantro when plated , Yum!

After cooking over 100 batches of 1# beans with lessons learned. I salt the soak water with 1 tbsp salt. soak 8hrs, drain, rinse, cover with 1" with water and bring to a boil (it takes about 15min). boil for 3 min. cover and turn to LOW. set timer for 1 hour. 30 min. in add 1 onion cut into 8ths don't add any salt. When timer goes off then check with a fork when pressed down the black beans should have no resistance. Overcooked and they mash to easy you want soft but not mush. 1 hour works only for small black beans larger pinto adds 30 min. Adding green peppers or poblano's are very nice. Thanks

I never soak dry beans just allow extra time in the slow cooker. 4 to 6 hours. Add salt after the beans tested tender.
Definitely skip the vinegar and wine. My first try was great tasting until I added the last 3 ingredients. Made them inedible.

Best black beans I have ever tasted. I omitted the green pepper (just a personal preference as green pepper just doesn't seem to agree with my stomach). Didn't soak ahead of time, just put them right in the crock pot as one reviewer suggested. Added salt from the start as suggested by the same reviewer. After 6-8 hours on low, beans were still "crunchy". Added 1 cup additional water and cooked for another 8 hours over night. Beans were perfectly cooked and tender. Stirred in white wine, vinegar and olive and cooked down a bit and the end result is really fantastic. Keep in mind that you are adding a full cup of liquid at the end. Therefore, you probably want the beans to have cooked down considerably before the last step.

First of all, I took the easy way out and used canned beans. I sautéed the onions, peppers and garlic in the olive oil, then added the bay leaf and seasonings. I also gave it a good glug of chicken broth to help keep the beans moist while they simmered (the truth be told a little bacon grease too!), and also added the wine at this point. The idea of adding the wine at the end without cooking off the alcohol didn’t appeal to me. Besides, simmering the beans WITH the wine helps give them good flavor! I did add the vinegar at the end, which really served to brighten the flavor as well. I simmered them about 20 minutes, basically the time it took to heat the chicken enchiladas I served them with. I liked these dressed up black beans and they worked well with the enchiladas.

Really great! Fixed 3/28/12: Used 4 cans of Bush's black beans....onion flakes....minced garlic. Cut salt to 1tsp....cumin and oregano to 1/2t....used cider vinegar, about 4t. Omitted pepper, wine and oil but might try them next time.

This tasted pretty good but it tasted best after it sat in the refrigerator overnight. I guess that gave the dish time for the seasonings to m set in. I used a red pepper instead of a green pepper because that’s what I had handy. I also added a lot more salt and pepper to the dish at the end which helped to bring out more of the flavors. This dish made a lot of beans. So next time I’d likely make only half.
I made it on the cooktop. Beans never got soft. I put chopped ham in the soup. Perhaps that was too salty to let beans get soft.
Delicious!! Made it as directed but.added leftover creamed corn, diced ham and vegetable broth. My husband loved it. Good with rice and hot water cornbread.
Would have been great... but then adding the vinegar & wine ruined it.

Thank you for the recipie. I have made this every 1-2 months for the 3 years, often a double batch. I never have used the oil or vinegar and have only used peppers a couple of times. I also add the same amount of ground corriander as cumin. I prefer the taste/texture when I add the salt after the beans have finished cooking. I mash the beans and put a single serving size in a ziplock sandwich baggie and freeze flat. When I want a bean burrito I'll take one bag out of the freezer, peel the plastic off the frozen slab, put it and a little water in a nonstick skillet then heat and reduce until desired consistency. Usually it is ready to eat in less than 5 minutes. Yum.
Easy recipe
It was excellent.
I cheated and used canned beans. Sautéed onions,peppers,and garlic in the olive oil. Added the cooked beans and simmered for 30 minutes. Then added wine and vinegar. Very tasty.
Great recipe. I substituted 3 cans of rinsed, drained black beans and halved all the other ingredients. Turned out great. Best black beans I ever made.
